response.initial_request: Please obtain a quotation for the maintenance items recorded at the vacant property following the move-out inspection. The property is being prepared for re-letting.

other_sections.Attachments:
- [Checkout Report — Move-Out Defects](attachments/checkout-report.pdf)
- [Alderwick Property Works — Move-Out Works Quotation](attachments/move-out-works-quotation.pdf)

events.body: Move-out list records damage to the staircase newel posts and a bedroom door frame; screw damage to an upstairs uPVC window frame; wall holes, plugs, nail holes and sticker residue; kitchen flooring damage and chipped living-room laminate with a missing threshold; missing downstairs toilet-roll holder, bedroom curtain pole and curtains, and some bulbs; a non-working top-floor smoke detector; a kitchen radiator pulled away from the wall; a warped kitchen worktop with reported water ingress; a boiler casing apparently held with tape and needing inspection; two reported non-working extractor fans; rusting radiators, including the en-suite radiator; ceiling or water-damage defects in the kitchen, lounge, Bedroom 3, bathroom and en-suite; altered decoration; and stained, faded carpets for which replacement was requested as a quote.
Workflow note says landlord approval is normally already in place for move-out works and the property is marked vacant. It directs the operator to check whether approval remains outstanding.
The full move-out list was retained as the job description. The property is vacant; keys are held at the agency office.

A handyman provider was selected and asked to quote remotely. The job email said the move-out works had been agreed with the landlord, and requested the provider's price, proposed work and earliest availability. It also offered access for an inspection if needed.
Advised that a provider had been asked to quote for the move-out works. No specific price or contractor scope was included in this update.
Asked for the property's check-out report before preparing the quotation.
Sent a check-out report in response to the request.
Followed up to say the report sent earlier was an old report from a different period and not useful for this job; asked the contractor to disregard it and sent the intended current report separately.
Asked whether the corrected report gave enough information to quote or whether an inspection was needed. Requested the quote and earliest availability while re-letting preparations were underway.
Call transcript records automated menu prompts only; no substantive conversation or agreement was captured.
Chased for the quotation and asked whether an inspection was required. Repeated that keys could be collected from the office.
Followed up again for the quotation or confirmation that an inspection was needed.

Sent a quotation for the property and invited questions. The listed tasks are: repair damaged newel post; address screw damage to a door frame; fill holes in uPVC window frames; make good wall damage; fit a new door threshold; fit a toilet-roll holder; renew smoke detector; rehang kitchen radiator; renew an extractor fan; renew en-suite radiator; renew an extractor fan; stain-block water-damaged ceilings; and reinstate decoration. The quotation text then gives a single “Labour & Materials” heading, without task-by-task prices or stated exclusions. Iris said she could not provide an attendance date at this stage and would only check scheduling after approval.
Forwarded the quote with a stated total of £3,865.68 and asked whether the landlord was happy to proceed at that cost.
Quote received; the stated total is £3,865.68 and is above the approval threshold. The workflow records that landlord approval is required before proceeding.
Waiting for the landlord to respond to the request to approve or reject the specific quotation.
Call transcript contains an automated recording notice and a brief unclear utterance. No substantive discussion, approval or rejection was captured.

args.reason: Waiting for Landlord (Owen Vale) to approve or reject quote NBL-027-Q1 (£3,865.68, VAT not stated) for 46 Fernwick Lane, Aldermead, ZZ1 1ZZ. It was sent on 2025-09-15 (event 14) and the call that day captured nothing (event 17). If there is still no reply, re-send or phone the Landlord. At that point also ask the contractor for an itemised breakdown with VAT and exclusions.

args.summary: The quote was forwarded to the landlord on 2025-09-15 and no reply has been recorded. Quote NBL-027-Q1 is £3,865.68, above the approval threshold. No contractor can be booked until the landlord approves. I sent nothing and scheduled a follow-up for 2025-09-18, with the reason "Waiting for Landlord".
facts: Quote NBL-027-Q1 from Alderwick Property Works is a single 'Labour & Materials' line of £3,865.68 (move-out-works-quotation.pdf, event 13)
The landlord was asked on 2025-09-15 whether to proceed at £3,865.68 (event 14)
The workflow says the total is above the approval threshold and landlord approval is required (event 15)
The note at event 16 says the agency is waiting for the landlord's decision
The call to the landlord captured no approval or rejection (event 17)
The contractor will only check scheduling after approval and gave no attendance date (event 13)
The property is vacant and the keys are at the agency office (event 3)
conflicts: Event 2 says landlord approval is normally already in place, but event 15 says approval is required for this quote, and event 4 told the contractor the works were already agreed. Nothing in the record shows approval, so I treated it as outstanding.

The quote does not cover every item in the checkout report: the worktop, boiler casing inspection, flooring, carpets, curtains and curtain pole, bulbs and remaining rusting radiators are missing (checkout-report.pdf compared with the quote).
The quote has no task-by-task prices, no VAT statement and no exclusions, even though event 13 lists the tasks.
The first report sent to the contractor was an old one and was replaced (events 7-8). The quote is dated after the corrected report was sent.
missing: Landlord approval or rejection of the quote
Itemised pricing, a VAT statement and exclusions from the contractor
Quote or inspection for the items the contractor left out: boiler casing, worktop, carpets, flooring and others
options_rejected: Booking the contractor: there is no landlord approval

Escalating: the landlord was only asked today and has not been silent for long. The conflict over whether approval was already given does not settle the next step, because the landlord can answer it directly.
Asking the contractor for an itemised quote now: I judged it premature, since the landlord's reply may settle the matter first. I will ask if the landlord is still silent at the follow-up.
Closing the case: no work has been done
args.uncertainty: The quote is lump-sum and incomplete, so the landlord may ask for a breakdown or a second quote. The boiler casing inspection is not covered and may need separate attention. The 3-day follow-up interval is the playbook default, not a date given in the case.
